name: What should be included in a luxury home construction budget in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: What line items should a luxury home construction budget include so I do not miss major costs in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What line items should a luxury home construction budget include so I do not miss major costs in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: A complete luxury construction budget should cover much more than visible finishes. It should include preconstruction design, engineering, permit fees, demolition, structural work, framing, roofing, windows, plumbing, electrical, HVAC, insulation, drywall, flooring, cabinetry, millwork, tile, paint, fixtures, landscaping, and final cleanup. Homeowners should also include allowances for appliances, lighting packages, specialty materials, site logistics, dumpster use, and temporary living costs if the house will be uninhabitable during work. In Los Angeles, budget overruns often come from permit revisions, utility upgrades, hidden structural conditions, and finish selections that exceed the original allowance. A reliable builder should provide a clear scope, detailed allowances, exclusions, and contingency guidance before construction begins. That level of detail makes it easier to compare bids and avoid surprises once the job is underway.
acceptedAnswer.description: A luxury home construction budget should include design, engineering, permits, demo, structural work, framing, mechanical systems, finishes, appliances, contingency, temporary living costs, and site protection. Missing permit-related or utility-related items is a common reason budgets run over.
